channel.title: Prokhorov® — Blog
channel.description: Notes by Artem Prokhorov on web design and development — how websites are planned, designed and built, and what each project teaches along the way.

item.title: Fewer Screens, Clearer Product
item.description: Before a product dashboard gets a new look, find the views people open every day and give everything else a quieter place.

item.title: Five Questions to Answer Before You Design a Homepage
item.description: Before you collect references for a new homepage, answer five questions in plain sentences. Each one settles a part of the page.

item.title: What a UX Audit Actually Finds
item.description: Your site gets visits and few enquiries. What a UX review of a live site usually finds, and a check you can run on your own site first.

item.title: How I Use AI in Design and Development
item.description: Where AI tools sit in how I design and build websites, what I still do by hand, and what to ask any designer who says they use AI.

item.title: Design and Development in One Pair of Hands
item.description: Hiring a designer and a developer separately, or one person for both? What changes when the designer builds the site, and when a team is the better fit.

item.title: How I Price Fixed-Scope Projects
item.description: What a fixed price for a website covers, my packages and payment terms, what the written scope says, and the questions to ask before you accept any quote.

item.title: One Page or a Full Site
item.description: How to decide between a landing page and a multi-page website by what you sell, where visitors come from and how much they need to trust you.

item.title: Structure Before Style
item.description: Why the first thing I send on a website project is a list of pages and a plain-text outline, and how to read it before any design starts.
